summary: Chiew Hui Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Ho earned a PhD at Stanford University (2004–2013) and served as Discipline Chair at the University of Sydney in 2013.

Chih-fu Li works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Li served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later as its honorary director after retiring in December 2006.

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. Tseng completed a PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn, also studying under Nobuyoshi Yamabe and Canshan Cheng, and joined the faculty of Fo Guang University.

Chihiro Nakayashiki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, having studied at Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University, Kyoto University, and Himachal Pradesh University. Academic appointments include JSPS fellow (2014–2016, 2019–2022) and visiting researcher at the University of Edinburgh.

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. Akamatsu was a professor at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku University (1943–1947), and Yamaguchi University (1950–1952).
Chijun Hamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute in 1978.

Chikafumi Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies. Watanabe earned a master's degree at the University of British Columbia supervised by Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Aklujkar, and completed a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura.
Chiko Corona is a Buddhist studies figure who received traditional instruction from Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, serving at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980).
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar (~1957–1959) and held a post at the British Library (~1965–1985).

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Thomé H. Fang, Bingnan Li, and Lobsang Palden Tenpe Dronme, taught at Chinese Culture University, and served as honorary professor at Griffith University and Queensland.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2009). Keng held faculty positions at National Chengchi University (~2010, 2015–2020) and National Taiwan University (2021).

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Shyu completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University (2008) under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indologist. He served as a professor at Presidency University and held posts at Bethune College (attested 1941) and Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat (attested 1960).

Chintaman Ganesh Kashikar (1910–2007) was an Indologist. He served as Assistant Secretary at Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1941) and as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, where he served as Director in 1996, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and under Soyen Shaku, Dozan Sugimoto, Nantenbo Nakahara, and Ryushu Hara. He held leadership posts at Soji-ji and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) works in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University (~1964–1968), Takenaka was an associate professor at Hanazono University (~1974–1989) and a professor at Tokoha University (~1989).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He taught at Otani University, co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921, and taught Keio Nishio and Genjun Sasaki.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Gakushuin University, University of Tokyo, and University of Vienna (PhD 1994), she held professorships at the University of Tsukuba and researched at Toyo Bunko.
